key_insight: GaMO uses geometry-aware multi-view diffusion outpainting to synthesize consistent novel views from sparse inputs, enabling substantially better 3D reconstruction when few camera views are available.
problem_solved: Improves 3D scene capture quality under sparse-view conditions by generating geometrically consistent additional views to augment reconstruction pipelines.
method: Geometry-aware diffusion outpainting conditioned on sparse input images and camera poses to synthesize large-field novel views beyond observed pixels.
Multi-view consistency enforced via geometric priors (pose/depth/epipolar-aware conditioning) so generated views align with real scene geometry.
Use synthesized views to augment training or inference for downstream 3D reconstruction (e.g., MVS/NeRF), improving completeness and fidelity from few inputs.
impact: Enables high-quality 3D reconstruction with far fewer captures, lowering acquisition cost and expanding applicability to AR/VR, robotics, and cultural heritage where dense imaging is impractical.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sparse input views + poses → GaMO diffusion outpainting → synthesized views → augmented 3D reconstruction
Before/after comparison: sparse-view reconstruction vs. reconstruction with GaMO-augmented views (side-by-side)
Geometry overlay: input view showing epipolar lines/depth cues and how outpainted pixels respect multi-view geometry
Icon set: camera (sparse capture), diffusion model, 3D mesh/point cloud to summarize stages
paper_title: GaMO: Geometry-aware Multi-view Diffusion Outpainting for Sparse-View 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Yi-Chuan Huang, Hao-Jen Chien, Chin-Yang Lin, Ying-Huan Chen, Yu-Lun Liu
